# === PCA (From Scratch) ===
np.random.seed(0)

# 1) Build a 3D synthetic dataset with correlated features
n_samples = 200
f1 = np.random.normal(0, 1, n_samples)
f2 = 2 * f1 + np.random.normal(0, 0.5, n_samples)
f3 = f1 - f2 + np.random.normal(0, 0.2, n_samples)
X_pca = np.column_stack([f1, f2, f3])

# 2) Center the data
X_centered = X_pca - X_pca.mean(axis=0)

# 3) Covariance and eigendecomposition
Cov = np.cov(X_centered, rowvar=False)
eigenvalues, eigenvectors = np.linalg.eigh(Cov)
order = np.argsort(eigenvalues)[::-1]
eigenvalues = eigenvalues[order]
eigenvectors = eigenvectors[:, order]

# 4) Project onto the first 2 PCs
X_proj = X_centered @ eigenvectors[:, :2]

# 5) Plot
plt.figure()
plt.scatter(X_proj[:, 0], X_proj[:, 1], s=12)
plt.title("PCA (From Scratch): First 2 PCs")
plt.xlabel("PC1")
plt.ylabel("PC2")
plt.show()

steps.description: You seed sampling and generate the supplied number of rows with three related features. f2 depends on f1, and f3 depends on both with added noise.
You subtract each feature mean and compute covariance across columns. eigh returns covariance eigenvalues and their direction vectors.

steps.answer: Sorting eigenvalues in descending order moves the largest-variance directions first. The projection uses the first two reordered columns.

steps.description: You multiply centered data by those directions to obtain two coordinates per row. The final scatter plot displays PC1 against PC2.
